claim: The legislature meets at noon on the second Tuesday of January in odd years for a general and budget session
quote: on the second Tuesday of January of the odd-numbered years for general and budget session

claim: It may meet in even years for a budget session
quote: may meet on the second Tuesday of January of the even-numbered years for budget session

claim: No more than 40 legislative working days in a calendar year, except special sessions
quote: The legislature shall meet for no more than forty (40) legislative working days excluding Sundays in any (1) calendar year

claim: A bill not returned within three days, Sundays excepted, becomes law
quote: If any bill is not returned by the governor within three days (Sundays excepted) after its presentation to him

claim: After adjournment the governor has fifteen days to file objections
quote: within fifteen days after such adjournment

claim: General elections are in November of even years
quote: on the Tuesday next following the first Monday in November of each even-numbered year

claim: The primary is the first Tuesday after the third Monday in August, for partisan and nonpartisan offices
quote: on the first Tuesday after the third Monday in August in general election years for the nomination of candidates for partisan and nonpartisan offices

claim: School and community college trustees are elected in November of general election years
quote: The election of members of the board of trustees of each school district and community college district shall be held for each district on the first Tuesday after the first Monday in November in general election years

claim: Trustees serve four-year terms beginning in December; no more than a simple majority elected at once
quote: Terms of office shall run for four (4) years beginning at 12:00 noon on the first day in December following the election

claim: Trustees are nominated by filing an application, not in the primary
quote: may be nominated for the office of school district trustee or member of a community college board by filing an applicatio

claim: Nominations by primary, petition or convention apply to all general election offices except school, college and special district offices
quote: except school and community college district offices and special district offices

claim: County clerks, treasurers, assessors, coroners, county and prosecuting attorneys, district attorneys, sheriffs and clerks of district court serve four-year terms on the 1974 cycle
quote: county clerks, county treasurers, county assessors, county coroners, county and prosecuting attorneys, district attorneys, sheriffs, clerks of the district court

claim: County commissioners are elected at every general election
quote: At every general election there shall be elected the necessary member or members of the Wyoming senate and county commissioners

claim: A board of county commissioners has three members, serving staggered four-year terms
quote: Each board of county commissioners shall consist of three (3) qualified electors

claim: Voters may increase the board to five
quote: any county may increase the membership of its board of county commissioners from three (3) to five (5) members

claim: A primary voter requesting a party ballot declares that affiliation; a voter may vote only the nonpartisan ballot
quote: An elector may vote only the nonpartisan ballot and if so, is not required to declare his party affiliation

claim: Requesting a party ballot is a declaration of party affiliation
quote: Requesting a partisan primary election ballot constitutes a declaration of party affiliation

claim: Party changes for the primary must be filed before the candidate filing period opens
quote: filing it with the county clerk before the first day on which an application for nomination may be filed

claim: Party nominees are the candidates with the most primary votes
quote: who receive the largest number of votes shall be nominated

claim: A losing primary candidate may not run by petition for the same office
quote: may not seek nomination by petition for the same office at the next general election

claim: Independent petitions for county office are signed by registered electors of the county eligible to vote for the candidate
quote: a petition shall be signed by registered electors, resident in the county and eligible to vote for the petitioner

claim: Nonpartisan ballots carry no party designations
quote: They shall contain no political party designations

claim: All municipal offices are nonpartisan
quote: All municipal offices are nonpartisan

claim: Municipal primaries and general elections are held with the statewide ones
quote: municipal primary and general elections are held at the same time, in the same manner, at the same polling places

claim: A municipality may instead hold its own elections in May every two years by charter ordinance
quote: which shall be held on the Tuesday next following the first Monday in the month of May every two (2) years

claim: All municipal candidates are nominated at the municipal primary
quote: All candidates for municipal office shall be nominated at the municipal primary election

claim: Twice as many candidates as seats advance from the municipal primary
quote: The candidates equal to twice the number to be elected to each office who receive the highest number of votes are nominated

claim: Special district director elections are in March, May or November, as each district decides
quote: shall be held on the first Tuesday after the third Monday in March or on the Tuesday next following the first Monday in May or November, as determined by the district

claim: In special district elections the most votes wins
quote: The person or persons receiving the largest number of votes is elected to office

claim: A first class city has 4,000 or more people and has been proclaimed one
quote: having a population of four thousand (4,000) or more which has been declared a first class city

claim: The mayor may be elected by voters or by the governing body
quote: means the person elected, either by popular vote or by vote of the governing body

claim: Cities and towns determine their local affairs by ordinance, subject to uniform statutes; no more than four classes
quote: All cities and towns are hereby empowered to determine their local affairs and government as established by ordinance passed by the governing body

claim: No more than four classes of cities and towns
quote: The legislature may not establish more than four (4) classes of cities and towns

claim: A city or town may exempt itself from non-uniform statutes by charter ordinance
quote: except as it may exempt itself by charter ordinance as hereinafter provided

claim: The constitution lets counties adopt township government by vote
quote: which may be adopted by any county whenever a majority of the citizens thereof voting at a general election shall so determine
